quote: This transaction is a 100% change of ownership of the Company. It squarely triggers §14.2. Vantrell's prior written consent is required. Yet **Schedule 4.4 of the Disclosure Schedule states "None"**—meaning Seller represents that no third-party consents are required (SPA §4.4)... If we close without Vantrell's consent, Vantrell has the right to terminate the Supply Agreement on 30 days' notice... Make Closing conditional on delivery of Vantrell's written consent to the change of control (this should be added to Schedule 4.4 and to the conditions in Section 7.2(c)).
reason: The memo quotes Supply Agreement §14.2: a change of more than 50% of voting stock is deemed an assignment, needs Vantrell's prior written consent, and allows termination on 30 days' notice. It says the 100% stock sale triggers that provision. It notes that SPA §4.4 and Schedule 4.4 ('None') do not disclose the consent. It also recognizes that §7.2(c) reaches only consents listed on Schedule 4.4, so as drafted that condition does not cover Vantrell's consent. It explains why this matters to the client (loss of supply, indemnity subject to the deductible) and recommends making the consent a closing condition. This matches the ledger's expected finding.
